findings.rule: Constitution I.1: a reason must not assert a fact absent from the resume
findings.trigger: Cited fact text contains a date such as 2015 and the model writes 'Led 5 stores' or '5 years': numbersIn gives '5', citedText.includes('5') is true because of '2015', and the invented number is returned. Likewise '10' passes against '2010' and '4' against '2024'.
findings.title: Number check is substring containment, so short invented numbers pass against any longer number or date
findings.proof: Test: MET match citing EXP-01-1 (fact text 'Cleaned weekly sales data for 40 stores', dates 2024) with reason 'Led 4 stores'; expected 'Shown in your resume', actual reason kept.

findings.rule: Constitution I.1 and issue scope: reason built only from cited evidence
findings.trigger: MET match cites skill:SQL and the model writes 'Used at Infosys and Tata Digital' or 'Led a team of five'; it has no digits, so reasonFor returns it unchanged although no cited fact names Infosys or a team.
findings.title: Only digits are validated; company names, tools, titles and number words in a reason are never checked against the cited facts
findings.proof: Test: MET with evidenceIds ['EXP-01-1'] and reason 'Used at Infosys and Tata Digital'; expected fallback phrase, actual reason returned verbatim. Upgrade path: require every capitalised token and number word to appear in citedText, or build the reason from the cited fact text server-side.

findings.rule: Issue AC: Northwind JD -> location 'Bengaluru · Hybrid'
findings.trigger: Northwind JD that says 'Bengaluru · Hybrid': prompt line 117 tells the model to return 'the job's city or region', so the model will likely return 'Bengaluru' and the AC value is not produced; no test or fixture pins this.
findings.title: Location prompt and the Northwind acceptance value disagree

findings.trigger: 40 requirements with up to 10 keywords, 400-char text, and a reason of about 25 tokens each plus location now sit in the same 8000 cap; a long JD can truncate the JSON, generateObject throws, the user gets a provider error and the claim is released but the ai_usage row is spent. Reason length is bounded only by the prompt (schema line 53 has no max), so the server fallback does not bound the output.
findings.title: Output cap unchanged while per-requirement output grew; no measured headroom

findings.rule: Constitution I.3: no fit, ATS or likelihood wording
findings.trigger: Model returns a MET reason such as 'Strong fit for this role' or 'Likely to pass ATS'; it has no digits and 20 chars, so it is returned. The prompt (lines 113-119) does not forbid fit wording and the server does not filter it.
findings.title: Neither the prompt nor reasonFor blocks fit/ATS/likelihood wording in reasons
